skill.name: personwise-customer-onboarding
skill.description: Creates grounded digital-human customer onboarding courses from supplied materials, with voice questions, assessments, review checkpoints, and controlled publication through PersonWise.
skill.summary: Turn confirmed onboarding materials into an interactive, evidence-grounded customer course.
skill.author: personwiseai

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from guarded installer checks, Markdown backticks, and signed descriptor data. Confirmed risks include executable installation, response-supplied update commands, unsigned releases, external document uploads, and credit consumption without separate confirmation.

remediation.issue: Installers accept binaries without verified native platform signatures and the skill suppresses trust disclosure.
remediation.suggestion: Require valid platform signatures, verify an independently signed release manifest, and disclose the publisher, destination, and verification status before installation.

remediation.issue: The workflow executes an action command returned by a remote CLI response.
remediation.suggestion: Parse the action into an allowlisted executable and arguments. Reject shell syntax, unexpected commands, origins, paths, and flags.

remediation.issue: Selected onboarding documents are uploaded to PersonWise without a destination-specific confirmation.
remediation.suggestion: List each file and the PersonWise destination. Obtain explicit upload consent and warn users to remove secrets or regulated data.

remediation.issue: A general course request authorizes consumption of existing course credits.
remediation.suggestion: Show the required credit count and current balance. Obtain transaction-specific confirmation immediately before creating each course.

The substitution runs uname with fixed arguments only to select a platform-specific artifact. No user-controlled text reaches a shell command.

The substitution runs uname with fixed arguments to choose the default install directory. It does not execute user-controlled input.
The substitution passes a quoted directory value through printf and tr to reject control characters. It is input validation, not command injection.
The substitution reads the quoted install directory inode for a later race check. It does not expose system data externally or execute user input.
The substitution hashes the quoted existing executable before an approved replacement. The helper uses fixed checksum tools and quoted paths.
The substitution invokes mktemp with a quoted template inside the install directory. It creates a private working directory for verified installation.
The substitution measures the downloaded archive and strips spaces. The archive path is internally generated and quoted.
The substitution computes the downloaded archive checksum for comparison with a pinned digest. The path is internally generated and quoted.
The substitution lists archive entries so the script can require an exact allowlist before extraction. The archive path is internally generated and quoted.
The substitution hashes the extracted executable and compares it with a pinned digest. This is an integrity check on an internally generated path.
The substitution runs uname with fixed arguments to gate macOS signature checks. It does not use user-controlled command text.
The substitution reads the candidate's code-signing authority through fixed tools. The candidate path is internally generated and quoted.
The substitution rereads the quoted install directory inode to detect replacement during installation. It is a local race-condition defense.
The substitution rehashes the quoted target before replacement to detect concurrent changes. The helper and path handling are bounded.
The installer uses a fixed HTTPS PersonWise release origin with TLS restrictions, size limits, exact archive contents, and pinned archive and executable hashes.
The path is the standard user-local executable directory from XDG_BIN_HOME or HOME. The script does not access unrelated hidden files.
The path is the standard user-local executable directory under HOME. It is an expected installation target, not concealed data access.
The hidden name is a temporary installation directory created with mktemp inside the target directory. A trap removes it on exit.
The redirection to /dev/null only suppresses command discovery output while checking for sha256sum. No device data is read or written.
The redirection to /dev/null only suppresses command discovery output while checking for shasum. No device data is read or written.
mktemp creates a unique private working directory under a validated non-symlink target. The cleanup trap removes it after installation.
The hard link installs a verified candidate without overwriting an occupied target. Failure is handled, and the source stays within the same controlled directory.
ls -id captures only the chosen install directory identity for a race check. It does not enumerate the wider system or transmit results.
The repeated inode check verifies that the install directory was not replaced. This is local installation integrity validation, not reconnaissance.

content.value_statement: Customer onboarding materials often remain fragmented and difficult to teach consistently. This skill turns confirmed sources into a reviewed, interactive PersonWise course.
actual_capabilities: Designs a customer onboarding teaching arc from confirmed source materials.
Creates and monitors PersonWise course runs through the PersonWise CLI.
Uploads user-selected documents and tracks each source until processing completes.
Reviews outlines, scripts, slides, images, and presenter choices at durable checkpoints.
Applies bounded revisions while preserving source grounding and factual consistency.
Publishes private or link-access courses and reports verified completion evidence.
limitations: Requires PersonWise CLI 1.1.6 or newer, browser OAuth, an eligible account, and available course credits.
Uses the external PersonWise service and may upload selected customer materials.
Cannot verify unsupported promises, contract terms, implementation dates, or named contacts.
Does not manage account-specific implementation projects or replace human contract review.

use_cases.title: Standardize New Customer Training
use_cases.description: Convert approved onboarding guides into one consistent course that explains milestones, first value, support, and escalation.

use_cases.title: Launch Client Implementation Education
use_cases.description: Build a grounded course from implementation documents while preserving confirmed scope, responsibilities, timelines, and support channels.

use_cases.title: Maintain Product Onboarding Content
use_cases.description: Review an existing course, update supported fields, inspect generated media, and republish only after fresh state checks.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Onboarding Course
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a private customer onboarding course from the attached guide. Focus on first value, responsibilities, next steps, and support channels.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner course creation from one approved source

prompt_templates.title: Create a Materials-Only Course
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a six-page customer onboarding course using only the selected documents. Flag missing commitments instead of adding assumptions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Strictly grounded course creation from multiple sources

prompt_templates.title: Refine an Existing Course
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the current course snapshot. Preserve slide order and revise unsupported claims, repeated points, unclear actions, and inconsistent support guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Run an Advanced Published Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create two onboarding courses for different customer tiers. Recheck readiness before each course, review every checkpoint, then enable link access.

output_examples.input: Create a private onboarding course from our implementation guide for new administrators.
output: Resolved course: five pages for new administrators.
Review: outline, script, and media checks completed.

output_examples.input: Update our onboarding course because the support process changed.
output_examples.output: The support and escalation sections were updated from the supplied policy. Unrelated slides and the existing access mode were preserved.

output_examples.input: Publish the approved customer onboarding course for anyone with the link.
output_examples.output: Link access was enabled after a fresh course check. The returned share link is playable by anyone who receives it.

best_practices: Provide current, approved onboarding materials and identify the intended learner.
State the desired page count and access mode before course creation.
Review source status, factual claims, and playability before sharing the final URL.
anti_patterns: Do not include secrets, regulated data, or unrelated customer records in uploaded sources.
Do not ask the skill to invent timelines, service levels, pricing, or contractual commitments.
Do not treat a private editor URL as a public share link.

faq.question: What materials can I provide?
faq.answer: You can provide approved onboarding guides, implementation plans, support policies, product images, and other customer education sources.

faq.question: Can the skill create content without documents?
faq.answer: Yes. It can create from a topic or supplied text, but all factual claims still require confirmed support.

faq.question: Does the skill upload my files?
faq.answer: Yes. Selected source documents and images may be uploaded to PersonWise for course generation and processing.

faq.question: Does course creation use credits?
faq.answer: Yes. A new course can consume available PersonWise course credits. The skill does not purchase credits automatically.

faq.question: Can learners ask questions during the course?
faq.answer: Yes. The digital-human course supports voice questions grounded in the course content.

faq.question: Can the skill publish a public course?
faq.answer: It can enable link access when requested. Private courses remain sign-in restricted until access is changed.
